question: Line-level DAF vs discretionary split at CFs that label DAF grants: extend the purpose-text test to every CF in the DAFRC panel (not only the top 100) and keep filers whose Schedule I purpose text marks DAF grants line by line (e.g. 'DONOR-ADVISED, …' at the Minneapolis Foundation, '…; DAF FUNDED' at the Community Foundation of Greater Birmingham, 'DONOR RECOMMENDED GRANT FROM DONOR ADVISED FUND' at Lancaster County CF); compare own-state shares of flagged vs other lines within each CF
conclusion_affected: Whether DAF grants are less local than discretionary grants inside the same CF (within-CF test of the cross-CF result)
rationale: Only 3 of 96 top-100 CFs label DAF grants; the within-CF comparison splits 2 to 1 (Birmingham 68% vs 99% in-state; Lancaster 96% vs 98%; Minneapolis 78% vs 72%). More labelling filers are needed before any within-CF claim

question: Panel version of the local-share / DAF-share relationship: compute own-state share and Schedule D DAF share of grants for the same 100 CFs in FY2021-FY2022 as well, and estimate a within-CF (fixed-effects) slope of local share on DAF share
conclusion_affected: Whether the cross-sectional slope (-0.25 own-state share per unit DAF share with size controls) reflects CF type (donor base) or changes as a CF's DAF book grows
rationale: The FY2023-24 result is cross-sectional; donor-base composition (national donors at Chicago, CFNJ) could drive both variables. The netpayout990 cache already holds FY2019-2024 returns

question: Correct or footnote the Community Foundation for Southeast Michigan Schedule D DAF grants: FY2022-FY2024 are filed negative (-$44.7m, -$64.3m, -$129.3m) while Part IX grants are positive; check the XML sign and whether DAFRC and sponsor-cost-structure.csv treat it as 0
conclusion_affected: Any sponsor-level DAF share of grants (sponsor-cost-structure.csv reports 0 for this CF)
rationale: A sign error in Schedule D Part I line 3 yields a DAF share of grants of -96%; this study left the covariate blank. sponsor-cost-structure.csv floors it to 0, which understates a top-50 CF's DAF payout

question: Schedule I attachments for four top-100 CFs: Hawaii CF, Sacramento Region CF, CF for Monterey County and CF for SW Washington file Schedule I only as an attachment (not itemised in XML) in FY2023-FY2024; obtain the attached grant lists from the PDF return (ProPublica/IRS TEOS PDF) and add their local shares
conclusion_affected: Completeness of the 100-CF local-share distribution (4 missing CFs; all mid-size and likely local)
rationale: 96 of 100 CFs are covered; the missing four are excluded by the itemisation rule of mission_net_payout.itemized

question: Recipient-HQ adjustment for CF local share: re-key out-of-state CF dollars to the recipient's programme location where the recipient is a national intermediary (fiscal sponsors, national charities using lockbox addresses) and test whether the DAF-share slope survives
conclusion_affected: Interpretation of the DAF-share slope as 'DAF dollars leave the community' vs 'DAF dollars go to nationally headquartered charities'
rationale: Out-of-state CF dollars concentrate in DC/NY/MA/CA intermediaries (P-NEW-GEO-01 §2.4); the local share measures recipient addresses, not where money is spent
